content: Neroli oil is a plant-derived essential oil that has a fragrance similar to bergamot. It is extracted from the blossoms of the bitter orange tree, scientifically known as Citrus aurantium var. amara or Bigaradia. The blossoms are typically harvested by hand during the late April to early May period. Due to the delicate nature of the blossoms, the oil is obtained through water distillation rather than steam distillation, as the latter would damage the flowers. By the late 17th century, Anne Marie Orsini, the Duchess of Bracciano and Princess of Nerola, popularized the use of bitter orange essence as a fashionable fragrance. She used it to perfume her gloves and bathwater, and since then, the term Neroli has been used to describe this essence. Neroli oil is characterized by its refreshing, distinctive, and spicy aroma, which also includes sweet and floral undertones. It is one of the most widely utilized floral oils in the perfume industry. Neroli oil is considered non-toxic, non-irritating, non-sensitizing, and non-phototoxic. It is a key ingredient in over 12% of modern high-quality perfumes. The oil blends exceptionally well with citrus oils, various floral absolutes, and most synthetic components available in the market. It is a classic and essential element in fragrance design and is among the most commonly used oils in the industry. Additionally, it is employed in flavoring (alimentary) applications, although its use in this context is limited. In aromatherapy and massage, Neroli oil is valued for its calming effects on the nervous system. Traditionally, it has been used not only to alleviate tension and anxiety but also to improve circulation and aid in the healing of thread vein scars. A typical solution for topical use involves mixing three to four drops of Neroli oil with one cup of sweet almond oil or wheat germ oil. To stabilize the solution, grapefruit seed extract is added. However, if the solution is intended for use on children or pregnant women, the amount of Neroli oil should be reduced by half.
